receipt.scope: Specification examples and generated stimulus; not formal equivalence or reset-kind proof.

module_behavior: Iterative AES-128 encryption sequencer (FIPS-197) with a valid/ready-style input and output; the handshake ports are plain protocol none signals. Blocks are 128-bit big-endian byte strings: byte 0 is bits [127:120]. Registers, all reset to 0: busy, out_valid, rnd[3:0], ct[127:0] (the state), rk[127:0] (the round key). Outputs, all views of registered state: in_ready = !busy && !out_valid; out_valid; ct; rk; last = (rnd == 10); rcon = 01, 02, 04, 08, 10, 20, 40, 80, 1b, 36 (hex) for rnd = 0..9 and 00 for rnd = 10..15. Neighbours: round_out = AES round of (ct, round key rk, final round = last); key_next = key-schedule step of (rk, rcon). At each rising edge with rst low, using pre-edge values: if busy: rk = key_next; then if rnd == 0 (key preparation) rnd = 1; else ct = round_out and, when rnd == 10, busy = 0, out_valid = 1, rnd = 0, otherwise rnd = rnd + 1. Else if out_valid: out_valid = 0 when out_ready = 1 (ct holds). Else (idle) if in_valid = 1: accept: ct = pt ^ key (initial AddRoundKey), rk = key, rnd = 0, busy = 1. key, pt and in_valid are ignored except at the accepting edge, out_ready only while out_valid. An accepted block takes 11 busy edges (key preparation, rounds 1..10) and out_valid with ct = ciphertext appears after the 11th; the next block can be accepted at the edge after the output transfer at the earliest. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
